class Solution:
    def longestPalindromicSubsequence(self, s: str, k: int) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        if n <= 1:
            return n

        # We only need two rows of the DP table to compute the results, 
        # saving significant memory and improving cache performance.
        # dp0 represents dp[i+1] and dp1 represents dp[i]
        dp0 = [[0] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n)]
        dp1 = [[0] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n)]
        
        # Iterate over the string backwards for the starting index
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            # A single character is a palindrome of length 1 for any budget
            for b in range(k + 1):
                dp1[i][b] = 1
                
            # Iterate over the ending index
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                # Shortest distance on a circular alphabet
                pair_cost = abs(ord(s[i]) - ord(s[j]))
                if pair_cost > 13:
                    pair_cost = 26 - pair_cost
                
                # Fetching reference lists directly avoids 2D array lookups in the inner loops
                left = dp0[j]
                right = dp1[j - 1]
                mid = dp0[j - 1]
                cur = dp1[j]
                
                # We limit the boundary to avoid IndexError if pair_cost > k
                limit = pair_cost if pair_cost <= k else k + 1
                
                # For budgets strictly less than the pair_cost, we cannot afford to match ends
                for b in range(limit):
                    cur[b] = left[b] if left[b] > right[b] else right[b]
                
                # For budgets sufficient to match the ends, we take the max of matching vs. not matching
                for b in range(limit, k + 1):
                    best = left[b] if left[b] > right[b] else right[b]
                    m = mid[b - pair_cost] + 2
                    cur[b] = m if m > best else best

            # dp1 becomes the new dp0 for the next iteration (i - 1)
            # The next iteration will overwrite values at index >= i-1 in the new dp1
            dp0, dp1 = dp1, dp0

        # After finishing, dp0 will hold the final results for i = 0
        return dp0[n - 1][k]
